characters: Sena: a bright fourteen-year-old Ghanaian JHS 3 Maths quiz champion returning to class with a warm cardigan and water bottle.
Ama: Sena’s loyal desk-mate, empathetic and eager to replace rumours with real science.
Fiifi: a curious classmate initially confused by neighbourhood myths.
Rahma: class prefect, thoughtful and fair-minded.
Dr Quansah: a friendly district hospital medical officer visiting for School Health Week.

narrationPlan.voice: Warm, supportive teen voices for Ama, Fiifi, Rahma, and Sena; clear, compassionate clinical voice for Dr Quansah
narrationPlan.pace: Empathetic, lucid, and reassuring (about 125 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with distinct, natural voices for each JHS student, teacher, and community specialist.
Pause for two seconds at each comprehension check so learners can reason before answering.
Never rush the final page: let the scientific and moral synthesis settle clearly.

music: Soft, warm piano and acoustic guitar melody expressing friendship, clarity, and dignity (placeholder)
culturalNotes: NaCCA CCP Alignment: Integrated Science (B9.3.1.1: Circulatory system and blood functions; B8.5.2.1 / B9.5.2.1: Non-communicable inherited conditions vs communicable diseases), Social Studies (B8.2.2.1 / B9.2.2.1: Strand 2: The Family—genetic counselling before marriage, dispelling superstitions), and RME (B7.5.1.1 / B8.5.1.1: Human dignity, empathy for the sick, and anti-discrimination). Note: The HbAS × HbAS Punnett square serves as a visual enrichment bridge to SHS 1 Genetics.
Dignity note: Page 1 states that Sena himself is open about his condition, so the health talk does not disclose private medical information. Never use this story to single out a real learner.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated JHS age band (Basic 7 to Basic 9) and BECE conceptual level?
Is anything here scientifically inaccurate, stereotyped, or unsafe for adolescents?
Verify the HbAS × HbAS Punnett-square ratios (25% HbAA, 50% HbAS, 25% HbSS) and confirm clear distinction between blood group and haemoglobin genotype.
Ensure Sena is portrayed with full agency, high capability, and dignity—never fragility or pity.

teacherGuide.overview: Replaces harmful superstitions around Sickle Cell Disease with crystal-clear JHS Mendelian genetics (HbAS × HbAS), circulatory biology, pre-marital genetic counselling literacy, and genuine classroom empathy.
learningGoals: Distinguish clearly between communicable (infectious) diseases and non-communicable inherited genetic conditions.
Construct and interpret a Punnett square for two HbAS carrier parents (1 HbAA : 2 HbAS : 1 HbSS).
Explain why both parents contribute equally to a child’s genotype and state the role of genetic counselling.
Practise practical, stigma-free classroom support (hydration, warmth in cold rain, shared notes, anti-teasing).

beforeReading: Clarify an everyday confusion first: ABO Blood Group (O+, A+, B+) is NOT the same test as Haemoglobin Genotype (HbAA, HbAS, HbSS)!
whileReading: Pause on Page 3 and have every student draw the 2×2 Punnett square for Mother (A, S) × Father (A, S) in their exercise book.
afterReading: Work out two more Punnett squares in pairs: (a) HbAA × HbAS, and (b) HbAA × HbSS, recording % probabilities for each box.
discussion: How does understanding recessive inheritance protect mothers and families from unfair blame and broken marriages?
reflection: How can our class make sure any student managing asthma, sickle cell, epilepsy, or a disability feels respected and fully included?

mathsExtension.task: In a Punnett square cross between HbAA and HbAS parents, what fraction and percentage of pregnancies are expected to be HbAA, HbAS, and HbSS?

support: Use two colours of bottle tops (e.g., blue = HbA, red = HbS) to model parent gene pairs physically before writing letters.
stretch: Research Ghana’s National Newborn Screening Programme for Sickle Cell Disease and why HbAS carriers historically had partial survival protection against severe malaria.

Note: The HbAS × HbAS Punnett square serves as a visual enrichment bridge to SHS 1 Genetics.
Dignity note: Page 1 states that Sena himself is open about his condition, so the health talk does not disclose private medical information. Never use this story to single out a real learner.
localiseThis: Connect respectfully with a Ghana Health Service nurse or Sickle Cell Foundation of Ghana educational leaflet.

factCheck.claim: Sickle cell disease is an inherited non-communicable autosomal recessive haemoglobinopathy (HbSS), not an infection or a spiritual curse.
factCheck.explanation: When two HbAS carriers reproduce, Mendelian segregation gives each pregnancy a 25% chance of HbAA, 50% chance of HbAS, and 25% chance of HbSS, independent of birth order.
factCheck.reference: NaCCA CCP Integrated Science B9.3.1.1, B8.5.2.1 & Ghana Health Service Sickle Cell Management Guidelines.
